chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When wealth is claimed against you and there is no right of his upon you, and he intends to make you swear an oath — if it reaches the amount of thirty dirhams, give it to him and do not swear an oath; and if it is more than that, swear an oath and do not give it to him.

key_terms.ادُّعِيَ: A claim is made (passive legal voice), referring to a judicial/financial accusation
key_terms.تَحْلِفْ: To swear/take an oath (jussive form of حَلَفَ)
key_terms.دِرْهَم: Dirham — a silver coin, the standard monetary unit in classical Islamic fiqh
key_terms.مِقْدَار: Amount, measure, quantity used as a legal threshold
key_terms.يُحَلِّفَكَ: To cause someone to swear an oath; to administer an oath (from حَلَفَ)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on swearing an oath when a false financial claim is made against you?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a practical legal ruling regarding false financial claims and compelled oaths. A threshold of thirty dirhams is established: if the amount is up to thirty dirhams, it is preferable to pay and avoid the sanctity of an oath; if the amount exceeds thirty dirhams, the defendant should swear an oath rather than pay a false claim. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the gravity of an oath makes paying a small sum preferable, while large sums warrant protecting one's wealth through oath.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from one of our companions, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘When there is a claim upon you for wealth, and there does not happen to be for him upon you (a right), and he intends that you swear an oath, so if it reaches a valued of thirty Dirhams, so give it to him and do not swear an oath, and if it is more than that, so swear an oath and do not give it to him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from certain persons of our people who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If someone brings a claim against you for a certain amount of assets which you do not owe to him, and he wants to make you to take an oath, if it is less than thirty dirham, you must pay and must not take an oath, but if it is more than that you can take an oath and do not give the asset.’”
